terms.sub: Vision: Retinal Layers, Rods vs Cones, and Phototransduction
clues: Located at the center of the macula lutea, it provides the highest spatial visual acuity in the human eye
Inner retinal layers and blood vessels are displaced laterally so light strikes densely packed cones directly
Its photoreceptors exhibit 1:1 private-line wiring to midget bipolar and retinal ganglion cells

terms.sub: Vision: Retinal Layers, Rods vs Cones, and Phototransduction
clues: Absorption of a photon isomerizes 11-cis-retinal to all-trans-retinal and activates transducin (Gt)
Activated cGMP phosphodiesterase hydrolyzes cGMP, closing outer-segment Na+/Ca2+ channels
Uniquely among sensory receptors, the adequate stimulus hyperpolarizes the receptor cell and decreases glutamate release

terms.sub: Vision: Visual Pathways, Field Defects, and Pupillary Light Reflex
clues: This classic visual field defect involves loss of both left and right peripheral temporal visual fields
It results from compression of crossing nasal retinal fibers at the optic chiasm
A pituitary macroadenoma or craniopharyngioma expanding upward from the sella turcica is the classic cause

terms.sub: Vision: Visual Pathways, Field Defects, and Pupillary Light Reflex
clues: Also called a Marcus Gunn pupil, it is detected on the swinging flashlight test
Swinging light from the healthy eye to the affected eye causes both pupils to paradoxically dilate
It localizes to an asymmetric lesion of the optic nerve (CN II) or severe retinal disease

terms.sub: Vision: Aqueous Humor, Intraocular Pressure, and Glaucoma
clues: Pupillary dilation in dim light crowds the peripheral iris against the cornea, blocking aqueous drainage
Patients present with sudden severe eye pain, halos around lights, corneal edema, and a mid-dilated fixed pupil
Intraocular pressure spikes sharply above 40-50 mmHg, threatening rapid optic nerve blindness

terms.sub: Vision: Visual Pathways, Field Defects, and Pupillary Light Reflex
clues: Bilateral small pupils fail to constrict to direct light yet constrict briskly during near accommodation
This 'light-near dissociation' results from a dorsal midbrain pretectal lesion
It is a classic neuro-ophthalmologic sign of tertiary neurosyphilis

terms.sub: Audition: Tympanic Membrane, Ossicles, and Impedance Matching
clues: The middle ear prevents ~99.9% of airborne sound energy from reflecting off cochlear fluid
It combines a ~17:1 area ratio (tympanic membrane to stapes footplate) with a ~1.3:1 ossicular lever ratio
Together these amplify sound pressure by ~22-fold at the oval window

terms.sub: Audition: Cochlear Mechanics, Organ of Corti, and Hair Cell Transduction
clues: Resting on the basilar membrane inside the scala media, it is the sensory receptor organ of hearing
It contains a single row of inner hair cells and three rows of prestin-expressing outer hair cells
Bending stereocilia against the tectorial membrane opens tip-link channels for depolarizing K+ influx

terms.sub: Audition: Cochlear Mechanics, Organ of Corti, and Hair Cell Transduction
clues: This potassium-rich (~150 mM), sodium-poor fluid fills the scala media and membranous vestibular labyrinth
Secreted by the stria vascularis, it maintains a +80 mV electrical potential
Its high K+ concentration drives inward K+ depolarization when hair cell stereocilia bend

terms.sub: Audition: Tonotopic Organization, Auditory Pathway, and Hearing Loss Tests
clues: Different sound frequencies maximally vibrate distinct positions along the cochlear basilar membrane
The narrow, stiff base responds to high frequencies (~20 kHz), while the wide, compliant apex responds to low frequencies (~20 Hz)
This spatial frequency map is preserved all the way to Heschl's primary auditory cortex

terms.sub: Audition: Tonotopic Organization, Auditory Pathway, and Hearing Loss Tests
clues: Abnormal spongy bone remodeling at the oval window immobilizes the stapes footplate
It causes progressive conductive hearing loss in young adults, often worsening during pregnancy
Weber lateralizes to the affected ear and Rinne shows bone conduction greater than air conduction

terms.sub: Vestibular System: Semicircular Canals, Otolith Organs, and Nystagmus
clues: Three mutually perpendicular fluid-filled loops (horizontal, anterior, posterior) detect angular head rotation
Endolymph inertia deflects the gelatinous cupula overlying hair cells in the crista ampullaris
They drive the vestibulo-ocular reflex to stabilize retinal images during head turns

terms.sub: Vestibular System: Semicircular Canals, Otolith Organs, and Nystagmus
clues: The utricle and saccule detect linear acceleration and static head tilt relative to gravity
Their sensory maculae are weighted by calcium carbonate crystals called otoconia
The utricle is oriented horizontally while the saccule is oriented vertically

terms.sub: Vestibular System: Semicircular Canals, Otolith Organs, and Nystagmus
clues: Dislodged utricular otoconia migrate into a semicircular canal, most often the posterior canal
Head movements such as rolling over in bed provoke brief (<1 minute) episodes of intense spinning vertigo
Diagnosed with the Dix-Hallpike test and cured by the Epley canalith repositioning maneuver

terms.sub: Vestibular System: Semicircular Canals, Otolith Organs, and Nystagmus
clues: It is caused by endolymphatic hydrops—excess endolymph volume distending the membranous inner ear
Patients suffer recurrent episodic attacks of spinning vertigo, roaring tinnitus, and aural fullness
Repeated episodes produce fluctuating, progressive low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss

terms.sub: Gustation (Taste) and Olfaction (Smell) Transduction and Pathways
clues: Located directly above the cribriform plate, it receives unmyelinated CN I sensory axons
Its spherical glomeruli integrate input from olfactory neurons expressing the exact same odorant receptor
Mitral and tufted cells project from here directly to the primary olfactory cortex without a thalamic relay

terms.sub: Gustation (Taste) and Olfaction (Smell) Transduction and Pathways
clues: Failed embryonic co-migration of GnRH neurons and olfactory axons from the olfactory placode causes this disorder
Patients present with congenital anosmia (absent olfactory bulbs) alongside hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
It is most commonly inherited in an X-linked manner due to ANOS1 (KAL1) mutations

terms.sub: Vision: Retinal Layers, Rods vs Cones, and Phototransduction
clues: This inherited retinal dystrophy begins with progressive degeneration of peripheral rod photoreceptors
Patients develop early night blindness (nyctalopia) followed by progressive peripheral tunnel vision
Fundoscopy classically shows mid-peripheral bone-spicule pigment deposits and attenuated retinal vessels
